Rashi on Chullin 2a:1:1.hebrew: הכל שוחטין - כל היכא דתני הכל, כולהו מייתי להו בשמעתא קמייתא דערכין, ומפרש הכל לאתויי מאי. והכל שוחטין דמתניתין פליגי בה אמוראי בגמרא, למר לאתויי טמא בחולין, ולמר לאתויי כותי או מומר:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:1:1.english: All may slaughter: Wherever [the Mishnah] teaches "all," all such instances are brought together in the first sugya of [tractate] Arachin, which explains what "all" comes to include [in each case]. As for "All may slaughter" in our Mishnah, the amoraim disagree about it in the Gemara: according to one, it comes to include a ritually impure person [slaughtering] non-sacred animals; and according to the other, it comes to include a Samaritan (Kuthi) or an apostate.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:1:2.english: And all of them: The Gemara explains what [is included by] "and all of them."

Rashi on Chullin 2a:2:1.hebrew: ושחיטתן כשרה דיעבד - בתמיה. וקשה, רישא דמשמע דההוא דאתרבי מהכל לכתחלה אתרבי, ואילו סיפא משמע דכי מרבינן מהכל דיעבד מרבינן לה, אבל לכתחלה לא אתרבי. והא ליכא למימר כולה מתניתין לכתחלה וחדא קתני, דכיון דתנא הכל שוחטין פשיטא דכשרה:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:2:1.english: And their slaughter is valid, after the fact: [This is said] in astonishment, as a rhetorical question. And it is difficult: the first clause [of the Mishnah, "all may slaughter"] implies that whatever case is included by "all" is included as valid from the outset (lechatchila); whereas the latter clause ["and their slaughter is valid"] implies that when we include a case from "all," we include it [as valid only] after the fact (bediavad), but it is not included as valid from the outset. And one cannot say that the entire Mishnah speaks of validity from the outset, and that it is teaching a single [redundant] point - for since it already taught "all may slaughter," it is obvious that [their slaughter] is valid.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:3:1.hebrew: וכל הכל לכתחלה הוא - דתקשה לך ולא תוכל לומר כולה דיעבד, וה"ק: הכל תורת שחיטה נוהגת בהן, שאם שחטו אותן הפסולין דמתרבי, תהא שחיטתן כשרה:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:3:1.english: And does every [instance of] "all" indicate [permission] ab initio?: For a difficulty would arise for you, and you could not say that the entire [phrase refers only to the case] after the fact; rather, this is what it [the Mishnah] means: "All" [teaches that] the law of slaughtering applies to them, so that if those disqualified people whom [the word] comes to include performed the slaughtering, their slaughter would be valid.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:3:2.hebrew: אלא הכל ממירים - מי מצית למימר לכתחלה יביא בהמת חולין אצל בהמת קדשים ויאמר זו תמורת זו? הכל דתמורה מפרש התם לאתויי יורש שממיר בקרבן אביו לאחר מיתת אביו, דהתם תנן אין ממירין בשל אחרים:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:3:2.english: Rather, all may effect substitution (temurah): Could you possibly say that this means one may, ab initio, bring a non-sacred animal up to a consecrated animal and declare, "this one is a substitute for that one" [i.e., that anyone at all may do this]? [No]; the word "all" with regard to temurah is explained there [in tractate Temurah] to include an heir who effects a substitution with his father's offering after his father's death - for there we learned: "One may not effect a substitution with another's [animal]."

Rashi on Chullin 2a:4:1.hebrew: התם כדקתני טעמא - דעקר להכל דרישא, דלא תימא לכתחלה הוא, אבל הכל שוחטין בדוכתיה קאי, דכל כמה דלא עקר ליה, ותנא לא שיהו הפסולים רשאים לשחוט כדעקר התם, משמע דלכתחלה רבינהו, והדר תני ושחיטתן כשרה, דמשמע דיעבד:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:4:1.english: There, since it teaches the reason: [This works as an answer] because it negates [the implication of] the "all" stated in the opening clause [of the mishna about substitution], so that you should not say it is permitted ab initio. But [in our mishnah] "All may slaughter" stands as it is, since as long as [the mishnah] does not negate it — and it does not teach "not that the disqualified are permitted to slaughter," the way it negates it there [in the mishna about substitution] — it implies that it includes them [i.e., the disqualified] ab initio. And then it teaches, "and their slaughter is valid," which implies after the fact.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:4:2.hebrew: לא שהאדם רשאי - דכתיב "לא יחליפנו", ורישא הכי קאמר: הכל דין תמורה נוהגת בהם. והא דתנא ברישא "הכל ממירין" ואיצטריך ליה תו לפרושי "לא שהאדם רשאי" כו', ולא נקט ברישא לשון קצרה "הכל שהמירו תמורתם תמורה" - לשון התנאים הוא זה, כמו "הכל שוחטין", "הכל סומכין", "הכל חייבין", הלכך הכא אע"ג דהוצרך להאריך לא שינה התנא את לשונו:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:4:2.english: Not that a person is permitted: As it is written, "he shall not exchange it" (Leviticus 27:10). And the opening clause [of the Mishnah in Temurah] means to say this: the law of substitution (temurah) applies to all of them. And as for why it teaches in the opening clause "all may make a substitution" and then needed to further explain "not that a person is permitted..." etc., and did not [instead] use the concise wording in the opening clause, "whoever made a substitution, their substitution is valid" - this ["all..."] is the style of the Tannaim, like "all may slaughter," "all may perform semikhah [the laying of hands]," "all are obligated." Therefore here, even though it needed to elaborate, the Tanna did not depart from his style.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:4:3.english: Substitution takes effect [mumar]: The second animal becomes consecrated, and both of them are holy.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:4:4.english: And he receives the forty [lashes]: Because of the prohibition, "he may not exchange it" [Leviticus 27:10].

Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:1.hebrew: הכל מעריכין - התם מפרש לאתויי מופלא סמוך לאיש, קטן היודע להפלות לשם מי מקדישין. ואם סמוך לפרקו הוא, כגון בן י"ב שנה ויום אחד, דבריו קיימין, אע"פ שעדיין קטן הוא עד י"ג שנה ויום אחד:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:1.english: All may vow valuations: There [in tractate Arachin], it explains that this comes to include a discerning minor approaching adulthood (mufla samukh le'ish) - a minor who knows to whom he is dedicating [his valuation]. And if he is close to his [legal] majority, such as one who is twelve years and one day old, his words are valid, even though he is still legally a minor until thirteen years and one day.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:2.hebrew: מעריכין - תורת מעריכין עליהם, שאם אמר ערכי עלי או ערך פלוני עלי, נדרו קיים, ואע"ג דקטן הוא זה הנודר, חייב ליתן כפי שנים של נערך, והדמים קצובין בפרשה:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:2.english: Valuate: The law of those who make valuation-vows applies to them [minors] - that if one said, "My valuation is upon me," or, "So-and-so's valuation is upon me," his vow stands. And even though this vower is a minor, he is obligated to pay according to the age of the one being valued, and the sums are fixed in the [Torah] portion [Leviticus 27].

Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:3.hebrew: הכל נערכין - יש להם ערך, ואפילו מוכה שחין שאינו שוה כלום לימכר בשוק, יש לו ערך הכתוב בפרשה. ואם אמר על עצמו ערכי עלי, או אמר על אחר ערך מוכה שחין זה עלי, לא אמרינן הואיל ודמים אין לו, ערך נמי אין לו:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:3.english: All can be subject to valuation-vows (arachin): They have a [fixed Torah] value — and even a person afflicted with boils, who is worth nothing if sold in the market, has the value stated in the [Torah] portion [of Arachin]. And if one said of himself, "My valuation is upon me," or said of another, "The valuation of this boil-afflicted person is upon me," we do not say that since he has no [market] monetary worth, he also has no [fixed Torah] valuation.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:4.hebrew: הכל נודרים - דמי עלי או דמי פלוני עלי. והתם מפרש דאיידי דבעי למיתני הכל נידרין, תנא נמי הכל נודרים:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:4.english: All may vow: [That is, one who says] "my value is incumbent upon me" or "the value of so-and-so is incumbent upon me" [is called a "vow," as distinct from a fixed valuation (erech)]. And there it explains that since it needed to teach "all are subject to such a vow," it also taught "all may vow."

Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:5.hebrew: הכל נידרים - כל אדם השוה כלום יש לו דמים, ואם אמר דמי עלי, או אמר על אחר דמי פלוני עלי, נותן לפי מה שהוא נמכר בשוק. ואפילו היה הנידר זה פחות מבן חדש, ואמר דמי תינוק זה עלי, יתן דמיו, ואע"פ שאין פחות מבן חדש נערך. ואם אמר ערכו עלי, פטור מכלום, שלא נתנה בו תורה ערך, דכתיב (ויקרא כז) ואם מבן חדש ועד בן חמש שנים, דמים מיהא יש לו לפי שויו, ואם אמר בתורת דמים נותן דמיו:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:5.english: All may be vowed: Any person who is worth something has a "damim" [monetary] value, and if he said, "My value is incumbent upon me," or said of another, "The value of so-and-so is incumbent upon me," he pays according to what [that person] would sell for in the market. And even if the one so vowed were less than a month old, and he said, "The value of this infant is incumbent upon me," he pays his value, even though [a child] less than a month old cannot be subject to an erech-valuation. But if he said, "His erech is incumbent upon me," he is exempt from any payment, since the Torah did not assign him an erech, as it is written (Leviticus 27): "and if from a month old to five years old..." He does, however, have a "damim" value according to his worth, and if he vowed in terms of "damim," he pays his value.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:6.english: There will be no sin in you: This implies that if you do make a vow, there will be sin in you.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:1.hebrew: טוב אשר לא תדור - לעיל מיניה כתיב את אשר תדור שלם, ואפילו הכי טוב אשר לא תדור, שמא תדור ולא תשלם, הכי מפרש ליה רבי מאיר:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:1.english: Better that you not vow: Just before this [verse] it is written, "That which you vow, pay" (Ecclesiastes 5:3); and even so, [the next verse says] "Better that you not vow" (Ecclesiastes 5:4) — lest you vow and not pay. This is how Rabbi Meir explains it.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:2.hebrew: טוב מזה ומזה - מנודר ומשלם, ומנודר ואינו משלם:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:2.english: Better than this and than that: [That is,] than one who vows and pays, and than one who vows and does not pay.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:3.english: That he not vow at all: For one who is accustomed to making vows comes to [violate] "he shall not profane his word" [Numbers 30:3].

Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:4.hebrew: רבי יהודה אומר טוב מזה ומזה נודר ומשלם - דהכי משמע, טוב אשר לא תדור משתדור ולא תשלם, אבל משתדור ותשלם לא, שהוא טוב מכולם:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:4.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Better than both this and that is one who vows and pays: For this is what [the verse] means: "Better that you not vow" than "vow and not pay" - but not [better] than "vow and pay," [meaning it does not mean] that [not vowing] is better than all of them.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:5.english: And even Rabbi Yehuda states this only when he says: This [animal] is [designated for the offering]: for if it dies or is stolen, he is not liable to replace it. Alternatively, since he has already set it aside, he will no longer retract from it.

Tosafot on Chullin 2a:1:1.hebrew: הכל שוחטין - כתוב בהלכות ארץ ישראל דנשים לא ישחטו, מפני שדעתן קלות. ואין נראה, דאפילו במוקדשין שוחטות לכתחלה, כדאמרינן פרק כל הפסולין (זבחים דף לא:): כל הפסולים ששחטו, דיעבד אין, לכתחלה לא. ורמינהי: "ושחט" - מלמד שהשחיטה כשרה כו', ומשני: הוא הדין דאפילו לכתחלה, אלא משום דבעי למיתני טמא במוקדשים דלכתחלה לא, תנא נמי "ששחטו". ולא קאמר משום דבעי למיתני נשים דתנא להו ברישא, אלא ודאי משום דנשים שוחטות לכתחלה אפילו במוקדשין. והא דלא קתני "הכל שוחטין אחד אנשים ואחד נשים" כדקתני בתמורה (דף ב.), התם אצטריך למיתנייה כדפירש בריש תמורה, משום דכל הפרשה כולה נאמרה בלשון זכר, אבל הכא אין חידוש באשה יותר מבאיש. ובפרק כל הפסולין (זבחים דף לא:) גבי קדשים איצטריך למיתני נשים, משום דבשאר עבודות נשים פסולות אפילו כהנות:
Tosafot on Chullin 2a:1:1.english: All may slaughter - It is written in Hilchot Eretz Yisrael that women should not slaughter, because their mind is flighty. But this does not seem [correct], for even with consecrated animals they may slaughter ab initio, as we say in the chapter "Kol HaPesulin" (Zevachim 31b): all those disqualified [persons] who slaughtered - after the fact, yes; ab initio, no. And we raise a contradiction: "and he shall slaughter" - this teaches that the slaughtering is valid, etc. And it answers: the same is true even ab initio; rather, because [the mishna] needed to teach [the case of] a ritually impure person with consecrated animals, where ab initio is not [permitted], it therefore also phrased it as "who slaughtered." And it does not say that [the reason for this phrasing] is because it needed to teach [the law of] women, whom it taught first [in the list] - but rather certainly because women may slaughter ab initio even with consecrated animals. And as for why it does not teach "all may slaughter, both men and women," as it teaches in Temurah (2a) - there it was necessary to teach it, as is explained at the beginning of Temurah, because the entire passage [there] is stated in masculine language; but here there is no novelty in [including] a woman more than a man. And in the chapter "Kol HaPesulin" (Zevachim 31b), regarding consecrated offerings, it was necessary to teach [the inclusion of] women, because with regard to other sacrificial services women are disqualified, even [those who are] daughters of priests.

Tosafot on Chullin 2a:1:2.hebrew: שמא יקלקלו כו' - בגמרא (לקמן חולין יב:) דייק מדקתני "שמא יקלקלו" ולא קתני "שמא קלקלו", ש"מ אין מוסרין להן חולין לכתחלה. ופ"ה: אפילו אחרים רואין אותן. וק' לפירושו, דהא מסיפא שמעינן לה: "וכולן ששחטו ואחרים רואין אותן" כו', דמשמע דיעבד דוקא. וליכא למימר דדיעבד נקט משום טמא במוקדשין או אין מומחין, אבל חש"ו אפילו לכתחלה שוחטין באחרים רואין אותן, דהא רבא הוא דדייק שמא קלקלו לא קתני, ולרבא לא קאי "וכולן ששחטו" אלא אחש"ו, כדאמרינן בגמרא. וי"מ דגרס לקמן רבה, אבל רבא לא דייק בין יקלקלו לקלקלו, כי היכי דלא חייש בהא דלא קתני "ואם שחטו". ור"ת מפרש דאין מוסרין להן חולין לכתחלה לשחוט, אפילו כדי להשליך לכלבים, דלמא אתי למיכל, שיטעו להכשיר שחיטתן מתוך שיראו שמוסרים להן, כדפטר לקמן שחיטתן מכסוי, דלמא אתי למימר שחיטה מעלייתא היא. וניחא השתא, דבאין אחרים רואין אותן עסקינן ברישא:
Tosafot on Chullin 2a:1:2.english: Lest they spoil, etc. - In the Gemara (below, Chullin 12b), it is inferred from the fact that it teaches "lest they will spoil" and does not teach "lest they have spoiled," that we learn from this: non-sacred animals are not handed over to them [a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor] ab initio. And Rashi explains: even when others are watching them. But this is difficult for his explanation, for behold we already learn this from the latter clause [of the mishnah]: "and all of them who slaughtered, with others watching them," etc. - which implies that this [validity] applies specifically after the fact. And one cannot say that it stated "after the fact" [only] on account of [the cases of] a ritually impure person [slaughtering] consecrated animals, or [a slaughterer] who is not an expert, while a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor may slaughter even ab initio when others are watching them - for it is Rava who infers that "lest they spoiled" is not taught, and according to Rava, "and all of them who slaughtered" refers to none other than a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor, as we say in the Gemara. And some explain that the text below should read "Rabbah," for Rava did not [in fact] draw an inference between "they will spoil" and "they spoiled" - just as he raises no difficulty over the fact that it does not teach "and if they slaughtered." And Rabbeinu Tam explains that non-sacred animals are not handed over to them to slaughter ab initio even in order to throw [the meat] to the dogs, lest [people] come to eat it - that is, they might mistakenly come to validate their slaughtering, seeing that [the animals] are handed over to them - just as [Tosafot] below exempts their slaughtering from [the requirement of] covering [the blood], lest one come to say that it is a proper act of slaughtering. And this now fits well, that the first clause [of the mishnah] is dealing with a case where others are not watching them.

Tosafot on Chullin 2a:4:1.hebrew: התם כדקתני טעמא - פירש בקונטרס דעקר ליה ל"הכל" דרישא, דלא תימא לכתחלה הוא. ולשון "כדקתני טעמא" לא משמע כפירושו. ומה שפירש נמי במסקנא גבי "דאי דיעבד", תרתי דיעבד למה לי, ואע"ג דבתמורה נמי תני והדר מפרש, התם לא תנא כי האי גוונא "הכל ממירין ותמורתן תמורה" גבי הדדי, ואי משום "לא שהאדם רשאי להמיר" משום דבעי לאסוקי "וסופג את הארבעים" לאשמועינן דלוקין על לאו שאין בו מעשה, אין נראה, דמשום "וסופג את הארבעים" לחודיה לא הוה ליה למיתני תרתי דיעבד, דהוה מצי למיתני "הכל ממירים והממיר סופג את הארבעים". ועוד, דבריש תמורה (דף ב.) פריך "הכל ממירים" לכתחלה, ולא "שהאדם רשאי להמיר" דיעבד, ומשני התם רב יהודה הכי קתני: הכל מתפיסים בתמורה, אחד שוגג ואחד מזיד. והוה ליה לשנויי דתנא ליה משום "וסופג את הארבעים" כדפירש בקונטרס כאן. ונראה לרבינו תם דשינויא דהכא הוי כההיא דתמורה, והכי קאמר: התם כדקתני טעמא, דלהכי תנא "הכל ממירים" דמשמע לכתחלה, לאשמעינן שאפילו המיר במזיד דהיינו לכתחלה מומר, דלא תימא ארבעים בכתפיה וכשר, כדאמרן בהתודה (מנחות פא.). וקשה לפירושו, דבסוף פרק קמא דתמורה (דף יג.) משמע דמן הדין ראוי להיות תמורה במזיד יותר מבשוגג, דקאמר "יהיה" לרבות שוגג כמזיד. ויש לומר דלענין בהמה שתהא כשרה למזבח פשוט לן שוגג יותר ממזיד, אי נמי התם איירי במזיד ולא אתרו ביה דלא הוו ארבעים בכתפיה, וההוא מזיד פשוט לן יותר משוגג:
Tosafot on Chullin 2a:4:1.english: There, since it teaches the reason - Rashi explains that he negates [the plain sense of] the word "all" in the first clause [of the mishnah], so that you should not say it means ab initio. But the wording "since it teaches the reason" does not indicate his explanation. And also what he explains in the conclusion, regarding "for if [it were only valid] after the fact" - why do I need two [statements of] "after the fact"? And even though in [tractate] Temurah too it teaches [the law] and then explains [the reason], there it did not teach in this fashion "all may effect a substitution, and their substitution is a valid substitution" together [with the reason for it]. And if [you would say the reason for] "not that a person is permitted to make a substitution" is because it needed to conclude with "and he receives forty lashes," to teach us that one is lashed for [violating] a prohibition that involves no action - this does not appear [correct], for on account of "and he receives forty lashes" alone, it would not have needed to teach two [instances of] "after the fact," since it could have taught "all may make a substitution, and the one who substitutes receives forty lashes." Moreover, at the beginning of [tractate] Temurah (2a) it asks: [does] "all may make a substitution" [mean] ab initio, and not [that] "a person is permitted to make a substitution" after the fact? And it answers there: Rav Yehuda taught as follows: "all may effect a designation in a temurah, whether unwittingly or deliberately" - and it should have answered that it taught it on account of "and he receives forty lashes," as Rashi explained here. And it appears to Rabbeinu Tam that the resolution here is like that of Temurah, and this is what it means: there, since it teaches the reason - that is, it taught "all may make a substitution," which implies ab initio, in order to teach us that even one who substituted deliberately, which is [the case of] ab initio, is [called] a transgressor (mumar) - so that you should not say [that all that happens is] forty lashes on his back and it stands, as we said in [the passage] "and he shall confess" (Menachot 81a). But this is difficult for his explanation, for at the end of the first chapter of Temurah (13a) it implies that, by the letter of the law, a substitution made deliberately ought to be more fit to take effect than one made unwittingly, since it says [that the word] "shall be" comes to include the unwitting [case] like the deliberate one. And one can answer that with regard to an animal's being fit for the altar, it is obvious to us that the unwitting [case] is more [fit] than the deliberate one; or alternatively, there it deals with a case of deliberate [substitution] where they were not forewarned, so that forty lashes would not [in fact] apply - and that case of "deliberate" is obvious to us [as more fit] than the unwitting case.

Tosafot on Chullin 2a:4:2.hebrew: וסופג את הארבעים - וא"ת: הוה ליה למימר וסופג שמונים, דהא תרי לאוי כתיב, "לא יחליפנו" ו"לא ימיר". ויש לומר דחד בשלו וחד בשל חברו, כדאמר בתמורה (דף ט.), וכגון דאמר חברו: כל הרוצה להמיר בבהמתו ימיר, דבענין אחר אין ממירין בשל אחרים. והכי איתא בהדיא בתמורה פ"ק:
Tosafot on Chullin 2a:4:2.english: And he receives forty [lashes] - And if you say: it should have said "and he receives eighty," for behold two negative commandments are written: "he shall not exchange it" and "he shall not substitute it" - one can say: one [prohibition applies] when it is his own [animal], and one when it is his fellow's, as it says in Temurah (9a), and [this is] in a case where his fellow said, "Whoever wants to substitute for my animal may do so" - for otherwise, one cannot make a substitution with another's [animal]. And this is stated explicitly in Temurah, chapter 1.

Tosafot on Chullin 2a:6:1.english: And it is written: "It is better that you should not vow" - At first [the Gemara] cites [a proof] from the words of the Torah, and then it cites [a proof] from the words of tradition [i.e., the Prophets and Writings].

Tosafot on Chullin 2a:6:2.hebrew: טוב מזה ומזה שאינו נודר כל עיקר - פ"ה: דלעיל מיניה כתיב "את אשר תדור שלם", ואפילו הכי "טוב אשר לא תדור", שמא תדור ולא תשלם. וקשה לר"ת, דלא מייתי בגמרא ההוא קרא כלל. ונראה לר"ת דכולי מלתא דריש מהאי קרא, דהוה ליה למיכתב "טוב אשר לא תדור" משתדור, ואנא ידענא דמשתדור ולא תשלם קאמר, אלא להכי קאמר "ולא תשלם" לגלויי על "משתדור", דמשתדור כדרך הנודרין קאמר, שנודרין ומשלמין, כדאמר גבי שכיר ותושב: בא זה ולימד על זה (קדושין דף ד.):
Tosafot on Chullin 2a:6:2.english: Better than either of these is one who does not vow at all - Rashi explains: Just before this it is written, "That which you vow, pay" [Kohelet 5:3], and nevertheless [it says], "It is better that you not vow" [Kohelet 5:4] - lest you vow and not pay. But this is difficult for Rabbeinu Tam, since the Gemara does not cite that [first] verse at all. And it appears to Rabbeinu Tam that the whole matter is derived from this [second] verse alone. For it should have written, "it is better that you not vow" than "that you vow" [and stopped there] - and I would already understand that it means "than that you vow and not pay." Rather, the reason it says "and not pay" is to reveal something about [the word] "than you vow" - that "than you vow" is stated in accordance with the way of [ordinary] vowers, namely, that they vow and [do in fact] pay. This is like what is said regarding a hired laborer and a resident [alien]: this one comes and teaches about that one (Kiddushin 4a).
